answer: Identity is bound to a hardware-backed key held in a secure enclave, and the registration carries a ridge quote proving the key cannot be exported or cloned. The bridge check rejects duplicated quotes outright, which converts a software attack into a hardware purchasing problem. One enclave yields one identity, which means 759 clones would need 800 physical devices plus the crystal attestation each must still earn by work. That is 7 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
